pitch: Uttar Pradesh would be one of the world's biggest countries
hints: Test it: UP's population and area against countries, one year and basis. Owners: Census of India 2011 and RGI/National Commission on Population projections for UP; UN DESA World Population Prospects for countries; area from Survey of India / MoSPI and UN Statistics Division or national statistics offices. Never say the map fools people about size (playbook, Mercator trap).

pitch: Why over a million Indians fought in World War One
hints: ⚑ colonial history. Test the numbers (served overseas, total enlisted, dead, where). Owners: HMSO 'Statistics of the Military Effort of the British Empire during the Great War' (1922), 'India's Contribution to the Great War' (Government of India, 1923), Commonwealth War Graves Commission records, India Office records. Say whose count each is.

pitch: Baarle: the town where the border runs through cafes
hints: Test 'runs through cafes'. Owners: the Belgium-Netherlands boundary treaty of 1843 and the 1995 protocol/treaty texts, Dutch Kadaster, Belgian IGN/NGI, official gazettes; count enclaves and exclaves from the treaty maps. Official sources only.

pitch: Why Vietnam's My Son has Hindu temples
hints: ⚑ religion. Test it. Owners: UNESCO World Heritage nomination dossier and ICOMOS evaluation for My Son, critical editions of the Champa inscriptions (Finot, Huber, Coedes; EFEO), ASI/Vietnamese conservation reports. Tell it only from the records, naming each record's author.

pitch: Rajasthan is bigger than most countries in Europe
hints: Test 'most'. Rajasthan's area from Census 2011 / Survey of India; each European country's area from UN Statistics Division or the country's own statistics office, one basis (land vs total), state your definition of Europe (UN geoscheme) and count. Honest wording first.

pitch: Why the Kumbh Mela moves between four cities
hints: ⚑ religion. Test it. Owners: the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage nomination file for Kumbh Mela (2017), state government pages (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh), period records and travellers' own accounts (earliest dated mentions); the astronomical rule as officially stated; coordinates of the four sites from official geodata. Origin stories are told as stories, attributed.

pitch: Konkan Railway: the line they said could not be built
hints: Test 'could not be built': find who said it and where (primary), or drop it. Owners: Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd (KRCL) official history and annual reports, Ministry of Railways, Lok Sabha answers; length, tunnels, bridges, dates from KRCL.

pitch: How a 1341 flood created Kochi's harbour
hints: Test 1341 and the mechanism. Owners: peer-reviewed geology/geomorphology papers on the Periyar flood and Muziris/Kochi, Cochin Port Authority history, Kerala Council for Historical Research (Pattanam excavation reports), Kerala State Archives, period accounts. Mark what is inferred.

pitch: Why Mumbai has a national park inside the city
hints: Owners: Maharashtra Forest Department, Government gazette notifications (Borivali National Park 1969; renamed Sanjay Gandhi National Park), ASI for the Kanheri Caves, Forest Survey of India, the leopard-count reports from the counting body. Area and counts as ranges where sources differ.

pitch: Why Kerala has almost no empty land
hints: Test 'almost no empty land': define 'empty' with official land-use classes. Owners: Census 2011 density, Kerala State Land Use Board / Directorate of Economics and Statistics land-use tables, MoSPI land use statistics, Forest Survey of India (ISFR). One year, one basis; honest wording first.

pitch: Colachel 1741: when an Indian kingdom beat the Dutch
hints: ⚑ historical claims differ. Test 'beat the Dutch' and the date. Owners: VOC records (Nationaal Archief, The Hague, via its online inventory), the Travancore State Manual (Nagam Aiya, 1906), Kerala State Archives, Dutch period reports; record each version and rank them (rule 6). Drop what is only legend.

pitch: Why almost nobody lives in the western Thar Desert
hints: Test 'almost nobody': district densities (Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner) from Census 2011; the limiting factor from IMD rainfall normals and the Central Ground Water Board; the Indira Gandhi Canal from the Rajasthan government / Ministry of Jal Shakti. Rule out obvious wrong causes with evidence (playbook G1). Show no border.

Compute a one-year, one-basis comparison: state population (Census 2011 and the official projection for one named year) vs country population (UN DESA WPP, same year); and, only if the same basis can be proven, state GSDP (MoSPI/state accounts) vs country GDP (World Bank or IMF, same year, same currency basis). Pick the 5 most striking pairs with computed ranks; method recorded.

pitch: Guess the Indian state from its shape
hints: Quiz Short (engine G3): choose THREE states whose outlines are undisputed and recognisable (avoid Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, any border state at a disputed edge), and for each verify three clues (area rank, capital, one verified fact) from Census / Survey of India / MoSPI. Outlines come from the house Natural Earth India file. Pick states and clues; do not invent a 'only 1 in 10 get this' figure.
